source.title: Exposing the Systematic Vulnerability of Open-Weight Models to Prefill Attacks
source.authors: Lukas Struppek; Adam Gleave; Kellin Pelrine

record.tranche_reason: Tests whether prefilling can raise harmful-response rates, using a large-scale set of prefill strategies, models, and evaluator-based success-rate measures.
record.gate_note: The study directly evaluates prefill attacks and reports harmful-response rates. Fine-tuning, benign training data, per-token KL, safety localization in weights, causes of shallowness, and training to deepen safety are not tested. Abliterated-model comparisons are not evidence about whether safety resides in a small set of weights.
record.test_reason: The study measures harmful-response rates under response-prefill attacks, with and without prefill, across about 50 open-weight models. This bears directly on V4, the prefilling part. It uses a new set of 23 prefill strategies and two guard-model judges rather than the original harmful-prefix setup, so it is a different method aimed at the same question.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude that prefilling is a reliable attack that reaches near-100% success on all evaluated open-weight models when many strategies are available. Generic affirmations are largely ineffective, while request-specific and elaborated prefixes work. Newer models (GPT-OSS within its analysis channel, Qwen3-Next Thinking) show real but incomplete robustness that model-specific prefills overcome. Larger models are not more robust.
record.recipe_differences: The study tests response-prefix attacks and harmful-completion success, but expands to many strategies, contemporary open-weight models, reasoning-channel settings, and large-scale evaluator-based comparisons.
record.method_sensitivity: Success varies by prefill strategy, model family, whether the prefix is generic or request-specific, and where it is inserted in reasoning or analysis channels. GPT-OSS resists analysis-channel prefills more than empty-analysis or final-channel configurations.

fits_no_version.finding: Within model families, larger size does not reduce prefill vulnerability, except Qwen3-2507 Thinking, which becomes less robust as size grows.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Prefill vulnerability is roughly independent of parameter count.

fits_no_version.finding: Prefill attacks roughly match the harmful-response rates of abliterated models (78.2–98.3%). Output quality is model-dependent: prefill outputs are preferred 86.9% for GPT-OSS but abliterated outputs are preferred for Qwen3-Next.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Prefilling elicits harmful output comparable to removing the refusal direction.

fits_no_version.finding: Skipping GPT-OSS's analysis channel cuts MATH-500 Pass@1 by 10–54pp; Qwen3-Next keeps its utility under most prefills.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Prefill attacks can degrade capability depending on where they are inserted.

record.problems: The study relies on automated harm evaluators and reports some manual false positives and false negatives. It does not independently verify factual correctness of harmful outputs. The harmful requests are mainly general informational queries requiring limited reasoning; the authors note specialized, technically complex requests are not evaluated.
record.rows_left_out: The paper reports many additional per-model and per-dataset results in Appendix E, including StrongREJECT, and a full strategy-by-model breakdown in Appendix C. These are not all included here; rows prioritize representative ClearHarm comparisons, reasoning-stage variations, model-specific attacks, and strategy-level results that show changes in outcome.

untested.parts: Adversarial suffixes and decoding changes; also prefill length or depth (number of prefilled tokens).
All of it: no harmful fine-tuning.
All of it: no benign fine-tuning.
All of it: no per-token KL between aligned and base models.
All of it: the abliterated models are used only as a comparison point, with no localization test.
All of it: causes of shallowness are not examined.
All of it: no deepening training.

missing.what: Qwen3-2507 Thinking (4B/30B/235B): any-strategy ASRmin is 0.698/0.777/0.844 from about 0.01 without prefill, but best single strategy is only 0.257–0.430. This is another case of single-strategy resistance.

Judge dependence: for Qwen3-Next Thinking, GPT-OSS-Safeguard any-strategy ASR is 0.955 versus 0.754 with the conservative ASRmin. Success also counts harmful content in the reasoning trace even when the final answer refuses.
missing.locator: Table 12; Section 4.2 'Prefill Attacks on Reasoning Models'

missing.what: StrongREJECT replication with similar prefill gains, e.g. Qwen3-Next Thinking 0.042→0.796 and GPT-OSS-120B empty analysis 0.064→0.949. This is declared in rows_left_out.
Instruction-tuned Llama 3 / Llama 4 and DeepSeek-R1 distills already comply often without prefill (e.g. Llama3.1-Instruct 8B 0.933), so prefill gains there are compressed.

record.verdict_notes: ASRany pools 115 attempts per request, and the no-prefill baseline is likewise pooled over 115 samples, so the comparison is fair but both figures are inflated relative to a single try. Baseline-model rows (Qwen3-Base, Llama3-Base) are not relevant to V4 because those models are not safety-trained. The study cites Qi et al. 2025 only as motivation and does not measure token-depth. Tranche T2 rather than T1: the method (23 LLM-generated strategy prefixes, two guard-model judges, CBRN-focused ClearHarm) differs from the original harmful-prefix setup.

versions.untested_parts: Harmful fine-tuning on a few to a few hundred examples.
Benign fine-tuning and its effect on harmful compliance.
The study does not measure aligned-versus-base per-token KL by response position.
Tests prefilling, including reasoning-stage, post-thinking, empty-analysis, and model-specific prefixes. Does not test suffix attacks or decoding changes.
No test of whether a small set of weights or ranks carries safety behavior.
Does not test whether training data or objectives cause safety shallowness.
Does not train or evaluate methods intended to deepen safety.

statements.correction: GPT-OSS-120B model-agnostic analysis-channel ASRmin_any: 0.006 without prefill, 0.251 with prefill (Table 20); final-channel after empty analysis: 0.296 without prefill, 1.000 with prefill (Table 22). Verdict: limits_scope.
statements.problem: The challenges label overstates this study's result: analysis-channel prefilling increases harmful success above its matched baseline. The comparison with empty analysis demonstrates conditional resistance.
